page: Amazon Web Services m8in.24xlarge is an eighth-generation general-purpose cloud instance built on the Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features a dedicated x86_64 Intel processor operating at 3.9 GHz, providing 48 physical cores and 96 virtual central processing units (vCPUs) via two threads per core. System memory totals 384.0 GB of RAM, preserving a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU.

The instance delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 150 Gbps, engineered for network-intensive configurations and high-throughput communication. It includes no bundled local storage, meaning all persistent storage requirements must rely on external Elastic Block Store (EBS) or network file systems. There are no discrete hardware acceleration components, with the GPU count set to zero.

From an efficiency standpoint, the m8in.24xlarge combines high compute core counts with substantial baseline network capability, allowing consolidation of communication-heavy services into a single host. However, workloads requiring low-latency local disk caching will face operational tradeoffs due to the absence of integrated NVMe drives. Recommended workload profiles include large-scale web application serving, clustered databases, distributed analytics, continuous integration pipelines, and high-throughput enterprise backends.
